moat_against: Commodity banking — no proprietary product; pricing power is the yield curve
Money-center banks and nonbanks compete for the same deposits and loans
Geographic concentration in the Southeast/Texas — a regional downturn hits the whole book
Earnings hostage to the credit cycle; current 42 bps charge-offs are the good part of the cycle
Regulatory capital caps leverage, payouts and achievable ROE growth
Multi-year record of muted net interest income growth versus peers
moat_for: Sticky low-cost deposit franchise — peer-leading 1.69% interest-bearing deposit costs (Q2 2026)
Scale across 15 Southeast/Midwest/Texas states with long-standing local relationships
Treasury-management and commercial relationships carry real switching friction
Hedging program supports top-quartile NIM of 3.66% and a mostly neutral rate position
Top-quartile returns: Q2 2026 reported ROATCE 19% (20% adjusted)
moat_justification: Durable, sticky low-cost deposit franchise in a 15-state Southeast/Midwest/Texas footprint (peer-leading interest-bearing deposit costs of 1.69% in Q2 2026), real treasury/commercial switching costs and a hedging program supporting a top-quartile 3.66% NIM and 19% reported ROATCE — but banking is a commodity business priced off the rate curve, with no proprietary product, geographic concentration, credit-cycle exposure and regulatory capital capping returns. Moderate/narrow moat: 5/10.
name: Regions Financial Corporation
one_liner: Solid, well-capitalized regional bank with a peer-leading deposit franchise, moat 5/10 — but on growth it actually prints (NII guided +2.5–4%) it does not clear 15% at $27.21: weighted IRR 11.2%, IV@15% $18.83; it clears the hurdle only near $18.83.
